problem:
Let $V={R}_{1}[t]$ be the vector space of all polynomials of degree at most $1,$ equipped with the inner product

$$
⟨x(t),y(t)⟩=x(1)y(1)+x(2)y(2).
$$

Normalize the  vector  $p(t)=2+t.$
worked_solution:
The norm of a vector $f(t)$ with respect to an inner product $⟨\cdot ,\cdot ⟩$ is defined as

$$
‖p(t)‖=\sqrt{⟨p(t),p(t)⟩}.
$$

Since $p(t)=2+t,$ we obtain

$$
p(1)=3,\,p(2)=4.
$$

Computing the inner product using our definition, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨p(t),p(t)⟩ & =[p(1)]^{2}+[p(2)]^{2} \\  & ={3}^{2}+{4}^{2} \\  & =9+16 \\  & =25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}‖p(t)‖ & =\sqrt{25}=5.\end{aligned}
$$

To normalize the vector $p(t)$, we divide $p(t)$ by its norm $‖p(t)‖:$

$$
\begin{aligned}u(t) & =\frac{p(t)}{‖p(t)‖} \\  & =\frac{2+t}{5} \\  & =\frac{1}{5}(2+t)\end{aligned}
$$
